sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-10-01-extension-scope2/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 23 (quality #22), Internal Quality Checks row 23 (no additional annotation); Quality Checks and Deterministic Checks sheets read, including deterministic runtime-deps row 32
evidence: PARTIAL runtime evidence, with no confirmed package/dependency defect. Frozen tests/Dockerfile:1-4 supplies Node 22 and Python 3.12; :16-22 pins Claude Code 2.1.281, Playwright MCP 0.0.79, Express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1; :31 pins harbor-rewardkit 0.1.7; :33-38 installs Chromium through the pinned Playwright dependency and provides /usr/local/bin/chromium. The verifier Dockerfile is byte-equal to the frozen template (SHA256 72998ab8ef0e4225e63b88fccdb754943c54022e25da355035efe7f759a55fdd); environment/Dockerfile:9-11 and solution/app/package.json declare the same server dependencies. I verified all 113 artifacts in current_golden and current_cli_admission against the then-current index (index SHA256 bfe7244648d7ce31bec231c48f53ded129981d4b9382b73600af8d022775c841), with no mismatches, and matched every CLI task/prompt/judge hash to the frozen task. CLI RESULTS.json explicitly says provider_invoked=false and judge_launched=false. Its Linux inert-exec admissions therefore do not demonstrate grading. The golden command runs launch_workflow.py directly and reports 119.594 seconds host duration, not test.sh or the configured LLM judge. My offline image smoke used immutable image sha256:46fefc505dbcabf0d6cb4e54fea8f0880acde2f7896587750af967427598977d and completed in 7.812 seconds: Node v22.23.2, Python 3.12.14, Claude Code 2.1.281, Playwright MCP 0.0.79, RewardKit 0.1.7, native SQLite query, app health 200 under UID 65534 from an outside CWD, Chromium 152.0.7977.8, visible app Run control, and synthetic browser click. See row22-tooling-smoke/observations.json (SHA256 f482247670bfc5de13dfb47a8f25fb649c7ba09bad67c82a381789b4950ad98c), command.json (9373ec93875009ad14d6d89dae4c38d8a9d52bfe22aea45255cd2c4ffe253a43), RESULTS.json (42f8c363da6e7f6e8474a787b820021d05028a7c6fdc04edf7e2b8f014352307), and verified artifact-hashes.json (all 10 entries match). This directly exercises the bundled Playwright library, not judge MCP registration or provider evaluation. Two prior diagnostic errors are preserved: /tests/Dockerfile is intentionally excluded by tests/.dockerignore:1, and an exact Run selector incorrectly omitted the keyboard text in app.tsx:149; the documented corrected selector matches the existing golden workflow selector. They are probe errors, not task failures. At review time runtime-evidence.json is absent and raw-evidence-index.json explicitly lists full configured judge completion/workload as unmeasured. No current full test.sh -> configured Claude/OpenRouter judge -> MCP -> serialized grade evidence exists; the smoke does not prove exact image build provenance or full grade capability. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:31 and qc/README.md:27-29 require that measurement and prohibit waiving it, so this row cannot be Pass.
counterexample: Evidence-sufficiency challenge (not a measured product verdict): a static app that serves /api/health and a visible Run button would satisfy this smoke despite dead execution/storage, while a fully conforming app could still receive no grade if provider authentication, judge MCP registration, or response serialization fails. Neither installed-version checks, inert argument admission nor scripted golden actions distinguish those grading outcomes; the configured verifier has not exercised them.
suggested_fix: When provider execution is authorized, run the unchanged frozen verifier end to end on this candidate, retain exact-image/source provenance and raw launch/MCP/provider/result logs, and bind the observed grading result and artifact hashes to this input_sha256 in runtime-evidence.json; keep the present smoke separate from that measurement.
